entity.name: iSRL (Lalitha A R)
entity.description: A computer once declared Maggi healthier than rice. We are an open research lab helping computers understand why the grandma will slap it if it says so — and hopefully make it learn Indian nutrition truth. We are process open, not just outputs. Lalitha A R is the founder and Principal Investigator of iSRL, leading all research, infrastructure, and contributor work.

projects.name: IFID — Indian Food Informatics Data (Core Infrastructure)
projects.description: A deterministic ingredient identity substrate for India's packaged food ecosystem. Uses the E-M-F Tri-Axial Identity Model to resolve ingredient identity across regulatory, trade, and common-parlance naming systems. Covers ~1,900–2,100 ingredient rows grounded in FSSAI regulations, ITC-HS nomenclature, and Supreme Court classification precedents. Designed as open data infrastructure — neutral, auditable, reusable by researchers, regulators, and public health practitioners.

projects.name: Identity, Transformation and Function: The E-M-F Tri-Axial Model
projects.description: A principled framework for assigning a determinate identity position to any food ingredient across three axes: Anthropogenic Energy (invasiveness of transformation), Matter (departure from biological matrix), and Function (degree to which technological role governs naming over biological origin). Derives a composite Divorce Score that partitions ingredients into variants, canonical entities, and functional tools. Validated against FSSAI regulations, ITC-HS, and Indian Supreme Court and Delhi High Court rulings. Includes a 35-item benchmark.

projects.name: Justification Companion to the EMF-Scoring Model
projects.description: Technical companion establishing the evidentiary framework for EMF scores. Synthesises chemical justification, FSSAI/Codex regulatory standards, and ITC-HS trade nomenclature to document identity shifts during food processing. Maps covalent molecular changes against statutory naming conventions, anchoring scoring assignments in global trade classification and Indian food safety law rather than subjective interpretation.

projects.name: Food Allergens in India: Evidence, Regulation, and the State of Current Knowledge
projects.description: A systematic review of food allergy in India co-authored with Dr. PA Mahesh (JSS Medical College). Documents a 136-fold gap between IgE sensitisation (19.1% in children) and clinical allergy (0.14%) — a structural finding that runs consistently across foods, study types, and populations. Reviews clinical and epidemiological literature, molecular characterisation of India-specific allergens, and the FSSAI mandatory allergen declaration framework. Proposes an extended allergen recognition list across two evidence tiers. Currently under peer review at npj Science of Food.

projects.name: Encyclopedia of Indian Food Ingredients
projects.description: A foundational taxonomy and multi-format dataset (JSON, Markdown, LaTeX) covering 600+ food components — from traditional Ayurvedic botanicals to modern industrial additives. Bridges traditional culinary knowledge systems with global food standards including Open Food Facts and INS/FSSAI classifications. Provides a machine-readable framework for food informatics in India, with nomenclature normalisation, hierarchical categorisation, and interoperable data structuring for API integrations and research applications.

projects.name: Indian Food Ingredients & Label Variants Dataset
projects.description: A structured mapping of 2,500+ regional ingredient variations as observed on Indian food packaging, linking label variants to standardised canonical forms. Built from 896 directly sampled products and OpenFoodFacts rows with traceable Indian product names, processed through a constrained parsing pipeline (temperature 0, explicit failure over approximation). The resulting 2,291 unique variant strings are documentation of how ingredient identity is actually expressed across Indian commercial food labels — ground truth for calibrating ML models and LLMs.

projects.name: Data Acquisition and Ingredient Extraction: Building a Vocabulary of What India's Packaged Food Labels Actually Say
projects.description: Documents the construction of the first ingredient variant corpus from Indian packaged food labels. Covers methodology, source selection, and the constrained parsing pipeline used to extract 2,291 unique ingredient variant strings from 896 sampled products and OpenFoodFacts. Frames variants not as noise but as evidence of how ingredient identity is expressed in practice — the question of which variants share an identity is addressed by the EMF model.

projects.name: Regulatory Texts and Case Law as Ground Truth in Emerging Domains
projects.description: A methodological note arguing that enacted law and judicial decisions constitute a practically available, historically grounded source of ground truth in domains where no unified academic theory has consolidated. Describes regulatory delta analysis — a method for reading how legislation and case law shift across time to surface friction points, coordination patterns, and the constraints under which each version of a rule was written. Grounded in IFID but intended to transfer to other domains with similar structural properties.

projects.name: Regulatory Delta of Food Labelling Laws in India: FSSAI 2011 vs 2020
projects.description: Summarises the regulatory delta between the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations 2011 and the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020. Focuses on the transition toward prescriptive naming, structured allergen declarations, and risk-aware warnings — and how these shifts directly inform field selection in digital ingredient identity layers like IFID.

projects.name: Indian Supreme Court: Hierarchical Classification for Food Products
projects.description: Synthesises landmark judicial decisions in Indian food classification law, documenting the transition from common parlance-based interpretation to a hierarchical technical classification framework. Analyses the January 2026 Supreme Court judgment in Commissioner of Customs Import v. Ms Welkin Foods, which established a precedential hierarchy prioritising statutory interpretation over lay understanding. Covers four domains: GST/Tax, Food Safety, Customs, and Dietary Labels — with implications for food informatics, regulatory compliance, and ingredient classification systems.
